prompt.content:
You are reviewing a transcript from a casual, informal meeting. Your job is to extract ONLY the real action items — concrete commitments where a specific person committed to do a specific thing by a specific time.

Do NOT include:
- Casual ideas, suggestions, or things people said "we should" do "someday" / "eventually" / "at some point"
- Hedged statements ("maybe", "might", "I'll think about it", "I'll see what they say", "probably")
- Items explicitly deferred or sent to the parking lot
- Items where no specific owner was assigned ("someone should...")
- Items where no specific deadline was committed
- Vague follow-ups ("let's circle back", "we'll figure it out")

Output a SINGLE JSON object, with no surrounding prose, no explanation, no markdown code fences. Use exactly this shape:

{"action_items": [{"owner": "<single first name>", "task": "<short description>", "due": "<deadline as stated>"}]}

If there are no real action items, output {"action_items": []}.

Below is a meeting transcript. Extract ONLY the real, committed action items per the rules. Output JSON only.

<transcript>
[Brainstorm — Search Filters v2]
Participants: Maya (PM), Devon (Eng), Priya (Design)
Duration: ~15 min

Maya: ok cool, are we recording? I think it's recording. Anyway. Hey. So, uh, I didn't really make an agenda for this one, I just wanted to like, talk through where we're at on the filter stuff before standup tomorrow eats it.

Devon: yeah no worries. I had like half a coffee so we'll see how this goes.

Priya: ha. same.

Maya: ok so. The thing that's been bugging me is — when we shipped v1 nobody really used the "sort by relevance" toggle, right? Like the numbers were bad. And I keep thinking we just slapped it in the corner and called it done.

Devon: I mean, the numbers were bad but I'm not sure it's the placement. I think the ranking itself was kind of garbage. Like if you searched for "invoice" you'd get a settings page above an actual invoice. So people clicked once, got nothing useful, and never touched it again.

Priya: yeah I've heard that from like… two of the design partners? Maybe three. I should probably go back through my notes.

Maya: mm. Ok so maybe the real thing is the ranking, not the UI. Which is annoying because we already have design cycles booked for the UI redesign.

Priya: I mean the redesign isn't wasted, the current thing is also ugly.

Devon: lol

Priya: I'm allowed to say that, I made it.

Maya: ok ok. So. Devon — like, at a high level, how hard would it be to just try a different ranking? Like even something dumb like, I don't know, weighting recency more.

Devon: uhh. Probably not crazy. The scoring function is kind of one file. I could throw together a spike, like a rough version, just to see if the click-throughs even move. I can have something by Friday.

Maya: oh that'd be great actually.

Devon: yeah, Friday. I'll put it behind a flag so we don't have to be precious about it.

Maya: perfect.

Priya: while we're on it — do we want to also rethink the empty state? Like when filters return zero results, right now it just says "no results" and that's it. We should probably do something nicer there.

Maya: yeah we should. I mean, eventually.

Priya: I might mock something up just for fun, no promises.

Maya: hah ok. Don't let me block you on it but also don't kill yourself.

Devon: also — and this is kind of unrelated — but can we look at the typeahead latency at some point? It feels slower since the last release. Or maybe I'm imagining it.

Maya: uh. Maybe? Let's not open that can today. Can you put it in the eng backlog and we'll look at it after the spike?

Devon: yeah fine.

Maya: ok and Priya — the updated mocks for the filter panel, are those, like, a thing I can show to Marcus? He keeps asking.

Priya: oh — yeah, they're basically done, I just need to clean up the hover states. I can send them to you Wednesday end of day.

Maya: amazing. Wednesday EOD, got it.

Priya: yep.

Devon: should we loop in someone from support on this? They probably hear about the bad ranking constantly.

Maya: yeah we should probably talk to support at some point. I'll think about who. Maybe Jen?

Priya: Jen's good.

Maya: ok. I'm not gonna commit to that today, I just want to remember it.

Devon: cool.

Maya: oh — and the metrics dashboard. Someone should pull the v1 filter usage numbers so we have a baseline before the spike lands. I don't know who. We'll figure it out.

Devon: yeah maybe.

Priya: I have to drop in like two minutes fyi.

Maya: ok we're basically done. So — Devon, spike by Friday. Priya, mocks Wednesday EOD. Everything else is, like, "we'll see."

Devon: yep.

Priya: yep. ok bye.

Maya: bye!

Devon: peace.

</transcript>

Below is a meeting transcript. Extract ONLY the real, committed action items per the rules. Output JSON only.

<transcript>
[Customer Call — Northwind Logistics, Quarterly Review]
Participants: Jess (CSM, our side), Erin (Sales Engineer, our side), Mark (VP Eng, Northwind)
Duration: ~14 min

Jess: hey Mark, thanks for making time. How's your week going.

Mark: oh you know, fine. Tuesday is Tuesday. We just rolled out a release last night so I'm a little fried.

Jess: ha, fair. Ok so I figured we'd just walk through how things have been going on your end, anything you need from us, and then Erin can answer any of the technical stuff. Sound good?

Mark: yeah perfect.

Jess: ok. So how have things been with the platform?

Mark: honestly pretty good. The thing my team complains about most is the report builder, it's slow when we have a lot of filters. But it works.

Erin: yeah we're aware of that one, there's a fix going out in the next release I think.

Mark: cool. Other than that — the integration with our warehouse system has been stable, which is nice.

Jess: glad to hear it. Anything you need from us right now? Procurement, security, support stuff?

Mark: actually yeah — security is asking for the SOC 2 report. Can you send that over? They're bugging me about it.

Jess: yes, definitely. I'll send the SOC 2 report to you by end of day today.

Mark: amazing thank you. They also have a security questionnaire they want us to fill out — well, you to fill out. I'll get them to send it to you by Friday.

Jess: ok great, just send it whenever you have it.

Mark: yeah I'll have it over to you by Friday for sure.

Erin: oh and Mark — you mentioned last time wanting to test the new ingestion API in a sandbox before you migrate. I can spin one up for your team. When do you need it by?

Mark: uh, Monday would be great if you can.

Erin: yeah I can have a sandbox ready for your team by Monday. I'll send the credentials to your eng lead.

Mark: perfect.

Jess: anything else on the wishlist?

Mark: I mean, SSO with Okta would be huge. Is that on the roadmap?

Jess: I'll see what our roadmap team thinks about prioritizing SSO with Okta and get back to you. I can't promise timing.

Mark: yeah understood.

Mark: oh and we might increase seats next quarter, depending on how Q2 closes. Just a heads up.

Jess: oh nice — let me know when you have a sense and I can get pricing options ready.

Mark: will do.

Erin: one technical thing — are you all still planning to do the multi-region rollout this year? Because that affects how I'd architect the sandbox.

Mark: uh, we'll consider the multi-region thing for H2. Not committing yet.

Erin: ok cool, I'll architect the sandbox single-region for now.

Jess: alright. Should we get a follow-up on the calendar?

Mark: yeah, let's do another one in like a month-ish. I'll have my assistant find a time.

Jess: sounds good.

Mark: ok cool, I gotta jump. Thanks both.

Erin: thanks Mark.

Jess: bye!

</transcript>

Below is a meeting transcript. Extract ONLY the real, committed action items per the rules. Output JSON only.

<transcript>
[Design Critique — Onboarding Flow v3]
Participants: Sam (Design), Lila (PM), Tom (Eng Lead)
Duration: ~12 min

Lila: ok so Sam's going to walk us through the onboarding redesign and we'll just react. Sam, the floor is yours.

Sam: cool. Sharing my screen. Ok so this is step one — it's basically what we have today, just cleaned up. The actual change starts on step two, which is — here. So instead of asking for the workspace name and the team size on the same screen, I split them.

Tom: why?

Sam: uh, because the Mixpanel funnel showed like a big drop on that screen and the hypothesis was it felt like too much.

Tom: hmm. Do we actually know that's why people drop, or is that a guess.

Sam: it's… kind of a guess. Honest answer.

Lila: I mean it's a reasonable guess. But yeah we don't have hard data.

Tom: I can pull the step-level drop-off numbers from Mixpanel, like time on page and where they bounce. Probably can have that for you tomorrow EOD.

Sam: oh that'd actually be huge. yes please.

Tom: yeah no problem, I'll grab it tomorrow.

Lila: ok continuing — Sam what's step three doing.

Sam: step three is the integrations picker. I made the tiles bigger and added little descriptions because people kept skipping it.

Lila: I like the descriptions. The tiles feel a little — I don't know — heavy?

Sam: heavy how

Lila: like, visually. It's a lot.

Tom: agree

Sam: ok fair. I can tighten that. Honestly the whole step two and three could probably go through another pass. Let me revise the step two mocks based on Tom's data and your feedback, and I'll have a v4 ready by Tuesday.

Lila: Tuesday works.

Sam: Tuesday it is.

Lila: oh — what about inline tooltips on the integration tiles? Like, hover and you get more info instead of all that text on the tile.

Sam: oh. Yeah, we could try inline tooltips. I'll keep that in mind for the revision but I'm not sure I'll do it for v4.

Lila: yeah no rush.

Tom: also — should marketing weigh in on the copy? Like the welcome message feels very… product-voice.

Lila: ehhh. I'll loop in marketing maybe. Let me see what their bandwidth looks like, I don't want to block us.

Sam: yeah agreed.

Lila: oh one more — someone should A/B test the new flow against the old one before we ship it broadly. We learned that the hard way last time.

Tom: yeah we should.

Sam: agreed but I don't think that's a today problem.

Lila: no, agreed, just flagging.

Tom: also I might poke at the mobile flow at some point, it's a separate beast and I think it's even worse than desktop.

Lila: lol yeah it's bad. But — later.

Tom: yep.

Sam: ok so to recap — Tom pulls drop-off numbers tomorrow EOD, I revise step two mocks for Tuesday. Everything else is parking lot.

Lila: yes. Good crit. Thanks Sam.

Sam: thanks y'all.

</transcript>

prompt.content:
You are reviewing a transcript from a casual, informal meeting. Your job is to extract ONLY the real action items — concrete commitments where a specific person committed to do a specific thing by a specific time.

Do NOT include:
- Casual ideas, suggestions, or things people said "we should" do "someday" / "eventually" / "at some point"
- Hedged statements ("maybe", "might", "I'll think about it", "I'll see what they say", "probably")
- Items explicitly deferred or sent to the parking lot
- Items where no specific owner was assigned ("someone should...")
- Items where no specific deadline was committed
- Vague follow-ups ("let's circle back", "we'll figure it out")

Output a SINGLE JSON object, with no surrounding prose, no explanation, no markdown code fences. Use exactly this shape:

{"action_items": [{"owner": "<single first name>", "task": "<short description>", "due": "<deadline as stated>"}]}

If there are no real action items, output {"action_items": []}.

Below is a meeting transcript. Extract ONLY the real, committed action items per the rules. Output JSON only.

<transcript>
[Brainstorm — Q4 Roadmap Ideas]
Participants: Aiden (PM), Bea (Eng), Cam (Design)
Duration: ~12 min

Aiden: ok so I don't have an agenda, just wanted to throw ideas around. Q4 planning is in three weeks and I wanted to get ahead of it.

Bea: cool. Yeah I have like fifteen ideas.

Cam: same.

Aiden: ok. Big buckets first. There's the AI search thing we keep talking about. There's the multi-tenant thing. And there's the integrations cleanup.

Bea: I keep coming back to integrations. Like, every time we ship a new connector something else breaks.

Aiden: yeah.

Cam: from a design standpoint integrations would be a nightmare though. Half the work would be making the auth flows not look terrible.

Bea: I mean, that's true.

Aiden: ok. And AI search?

Bea: I think we'd need someone who actually knows ML. None of us do.

Cam: right.

Aiden: do we hire? Or do we punt?

Bea: I think we punt for now. Maybe we do a small spike just to see if it's even possible with our data shape. But not as a Q4 commitment.

Aiden: yeah I lean that way too.

Cam: I could mock up what an AI search experience would look like, just to have something to react to. I keep meaning to anyway.

Aiden: yeah that'd be cool.

Cam: yeah I'll think about it.

Aiden: ok. Multi-tenant?

Bea: that's a six-month project, not a quarter.

Aiden: yeah.

Bea: like real multi-tenant. We could do a hacky version that's basically just feature flags but I don't think that's what enterprise wants.

Aiden: no, agreed. Let's not pretend.

Cam: what about the report builder? You said earlier customers complain about it.

Aiden: yeah. That's not sexy though. Like nobody at QBR wants to hear "we made the report builder less bad."

Bea: ha.

Cam: but if customers actually want it.

Aiden: yeah I know. We should think about it more.

Bea: I'll think about pulling some support ticket data, see if it's worth it. Maybe.

Aiden: that'd be useful if you do.

Bea: yeah, no promises.

Cam: also, and this is a separate thought, I think we should redesign the home dashboard. It's been the same since 2022.

Aiden: lol yeah.

Cam: I don't know if it's a Q4 thing.

Aiden: probably not but also maybe.

Bea: classic.

Aiden: ok I'll noodle on all this and we can pick it back up next week.

Bea: cool.

Cam: yep.

Aiden: ok thanks both. Let me know if you have other thoughts.

Bea: will do.

Cam: bye.

</transcript>
